about: Every departure from the server guide that the Brennan's pack makes, each with its reason and its source, so a reader can audit the pack against the guide (house/brennans/guide.txt, menus read 26 September 2026) and the research under house/brennans/research/. The builder (house/build-brennans.mjs) applies the entries in order after parsing and before dash stripping; a replace whose 'from' is not found fails the build. Verdict ids (chef-dishes-b-4, gap-pron-6 and so on) are the ids in research/verified-facts.json; 'pdf-corrections pN' points at research/pdf-corrections.json by page. A still-unverifiable fact is placed nowhere as a fact; a refuted claim appears only as its correction. Prices are never touched here. principles.reason: The guide prints five pairing principles outside the engine's nine. entries.value: Owen Brennan opened the restaurant on Bourbon Street in July 1946, and it has been at 417 Royal Street since 1956. Owen died in November 1955, before the move; Ella Brennan found the backing and the family opened Royal Street in 1956. The building dates from 1795, was the first bank in Louisiana and later the home of Paul Morphy, the chess champion; the bank's initials survive in the balcony ironwork. The family split in November 1973, settled in 1974: Owen's widow Maude and sons Pip, Jimmy and Ted kept Royal Street, and Ella's side took Commander's Palace. Brennan's closed in June 2013 and reopened in November 2014 under Ralph Brennan and Terry White after a restoration of the whole house. Paul Blange, the first chef, created Bananas Foster and Eggs Hussarde; Michael Roussel, Lazone Randolph, Slade Rushing and Ryan Hacker followed him, and Kris Padalino has led the kitchen since June 2025. 2026 is the 80th year.

entries.value: Invented here in 1951, when Owen Brennan asked his sister Ella and chef Paul Blange for a banana dessert, and named for his friend Richard Foster, chairman of the New Orleans Crime Commission (also called the Metropolitan Crime Commission). New Orleans was then the main port for bananas from Central America. Butter, light brown sugar and cinnamon, banana liqueur, then the bananas, then aged rum set alight at the table, over housemade vanilla ice cream.

entries.value: Eggs Sardou was created at Antoine's, usually dated 1908, for the French playwright Victorien Sardou. The original was poached eggs on artichoke bottoms with hollandaise, anchovy, ham and truffle, with no spinach. The creamed spinach most kitchens use now came later. Ours fries the artichokes, makes the spinach with Parmesan and swaps hollandaise for Choron, a bearnaise with tomato.

entries.value: Debris, DAY-bree, is the New Orleans word for the shreds of slow cooked meat that fall into their own gravy. Mother's on Poydras Street, open since 1938, made the word famous: its story is that founder Simon Landry asked a customer whether he wanted some of the debris from the roast beef carving board. Ours is short rib braised in red wine until it falls apart.

value.q: Is Eggs Owen named for Owen Brennan?
value.a: Owen Brennan opened the restaurant in 1946 and died in 1955. Do not say Eggs Owen is named for him unless a manager confirms it; the menu does not say. Eggs Owen today is short rib braised in red wine until it falls apart, over a Creole spiced potato, with a soft boiled egg and the same two sauces as the Hussarde. Use the current menu wording only; older write ups describe a poached egg and hash version that is gone.

entries.value: Grand Isle Jewels are farmed oysters from Grand Isle on the Louisiana coast, raised in floating cages above the seabed and tumbled so they grow a deep cup and a clean shell. The brand brought the island's farmers together in 2025 and honors the late Jules Melancon, the first permitted to farm off bottom in 2012; the menu's singular Jewel is the plural brand Jewels. Clean, briny and cold, served raw with a preserved Fresno chili mignonette.

If it is a special occasion, we pour Rare by the glass: Piper-Heidsieck's prestige vintage Champagne, Chardonnay-led from Grand Cru vineyards, kept fresh under a Coravin Sparkling stopper. It has the chalky precision raw oysters love, with toasted almond on the finish.

value.q: Catalina Island or Black Hills with the raw oysters?
value.a: Keep the guide's Catalina Island as the printed pick: the mignonette already supplies acid and the tonic supplies the one thing the plate lacks, bubbles. A server may offer the Black Hills to a guest who wants lime and basil with the mignonette. Test both at lineup. Fresno is a red Californian chili from the 1950s, about the heat of a jalapeno but fruitier and thinner walled; preserved and stirred into the mignonette it gives a gentle warmth, not real heat.

value.q: The cellar dossier's second opinion on the pairing?
value.a: Confirmed: salt and acid. The salt makes the wine taste fuller and the bubbles keep the oyster fresh. A chalky, Chardonnay-led vintage Champagne is a standard oyster step up, so the Rare stays.

value.q: What is the classic Sazerac build, and is it ours?
value.a: The Classic Sazerac at Brennan's is Sazerac rye stirred with Peychaud's bitters, served without ice in a glass rinsed with Herbsaint (ERB-saint), $13; confirm sugar and lemon peel with the bar. The Sazerac Company's own recipe is a sugar cube, three dashes of Peychaud's, an ounce and a half of Sazerac Rye, a quarter ounce of Herbsaint and a lemon peel, built across two glasses and served neat in a chilled rocks glass; the IBA version is Cognac based with absinthe. Give those as the classic, never as the house build. If a guest asks for it on the rocks, check with the bar before promising it. Two luxury versions: Thompson's Dream with Willett rye, and Origin Story with Cognac and absinthe; the price ladder is $13, $20 and $40.

entries.value: Owen Brennan died in 1955; the family opened Royal Street in 1956. Brennan's closed in 2013 and reopened in November 2014 under Ralph Brennan and Terry White.

value.title: The chefs
value.body: Paul Blangé, the chef behind Bananas Foster, led the kitchen until the 1970s. Michael Roussel, who started here in 1956 and trained under Blangé, became executive chef in 1974 and retired in 2005 after 49 years. Lazone Randolph, who began as a dishwasher in 1965, succeeded him in 2005 and gave his name to Chicken Lazone. Slade Rushing ran the kitchen from the 2014 reopening to 2019 and Ryan Hacker from late 2019 to spring 2025. Our executive chef is Kris Padalino, who took over in June 2025 after eight years in this kitchen as pastry chef and executive sous chef; she trained at Le Cordon Bleu in Pasadena and cooked in Los Angeles and Denver before New Orleans.

value.title: The building and the family
value.body: 1795: it was Louisiana's first bank, then the home of Paul Morphy, the chess champion; look for the bank's initials in the balcony ironwork. Owen Brennan opened on Bourbon Street in July 1946 and the house moved here in 1956, after Owen's death in November 1955, with Ella Brennan finding the backing. The family split in November 1973, settled in 1974: Owen's side kept Royal Street, Ella's side took Commander's Palace; Brennan's of Houston belongs to Ella's side, so a guest who ate at Brennan's in Houston ate at a cousin. The house closed on 28 June 2013 and reopened on 25 November 2014 under Ralph Brennan and Terry White after seventeen months of restoration.

value.title: The courtyard turtles
value.body: Ten turtles were found living in the courtyard during the 2014 renovation and adopted; Slade Rushing named them for sauces: Béchamel, Hollandaise, Espagnole, Tomate and Velouté, then Rémoulade, Ravigote, Bordelaise, Mignonette and Cocktail, the only male. Their return to the fountain in 2015 began the annual Slowest Second Line on Earth. Say it before the guest asks: the turtle soup is not the turtles.

entries.source: dossier-the-kitchen section 1 (house press release; Axios New Orleans 1 May 2026)

value.title: The by-the-glass list
value.body: Our by-the-glass list runs to twenty wines: thirteen glass pours from $14 to $75, an $80 half-bottle of Mosel Auslese for dessert, and six wines poured only as part of the tasting menus. If a guest wants one of the tasting wines on its own, ask before promising it. Check the list you are handed on shift: the website shows an older one.

value.title: The wine team
value.body: Our wine director is Sam Bortugno, an Advanced Sommelier, in post since September 2023; confirm at lineup that he is on the floor tonight and how to call a sommelier to a table. Braithe Gill is beverage director for the Ralph Brennan Restaurant Group, a certified sommelier and a 2026 James Beard semifinalist; the research also recorded her as Braithe Tidwell, who led the programme when the Grand Award was regained in 2021, so do not call her the wine director.

value.title: The Wine Room and private events
value.body: The Wine Room is our smallest private room, seating 16, in the old carriage house and stables beside the cellar, with a sixteen foot table milled from one sinker cypress; bookings go through the events office on 504-934-3376, with a minimum that depends on the date. Nine bookable spaces, seated and reception: King's 36 and 40, Queen's 24 and 30, Havana 60 and 75, Morphy 12 and 12, Chanteclair 100 and 160, Roost Bar 20 and 30, Audubon 50 and 60, Wine Room 16 and 16, Courtyard 50 and 75; events from 15 to 500. For private parties, corkage is $25 a bottle, a magnum $50 counting as two, six bottles at most; the dining room policy is not published, ask a manager.

value.title: Reservations
value.body: Reservations are on OpenTable, open 60 days ahead; parties larger than six ring 504-525-9711.

value.title: Parking and the street
value.body: Royal Street is a pedestrian mall from 11 in the morning, so there is no drop off at the door at lunch; the street is open to cars when breakfast opens and all evening. We validate parking at two garages, 535 Chartres and 716 Iberville, for up to three hours; check the current rates and whether valet is on tonight with the host stand, since the two readings of the FAQ disagree on valet.

value.title: Holidays
value.body: Christmas Eve: breakfast and lunch à la carte, dinner 5:30 to 9 with a three course $85 menu. New Year's Eve: breakfast and lunch à la carte, dinner 6 to 10 à la carte. The year is unconfirmed; re-read each season. Réveillon proper is advertised at the sister house Ralph's on the Park; Brennan's frames Christmas Eve as its holiday dinner.

value.title: The Ralph Brennan Restaurant Group
value.body: The group runs Brennan's, Napoleon House, Red Fish Grill, Ralph's on the Park, Cafe NOMA, Jazz Kitchen Coastal Grill and Patio, and Beignets Expressed.

value.title: Who does what on the floor

Erick Schmitt is general manager per the house's 2026 team directory; confirm the spelling on the page. Who performs the flambé, the Friday sabrage, the Chateaubriand carving, the papillote opening and the Coravin pours, and how the floor is organised, are lineup questions.

value.title: The children's menu
value.body: For children ten and under, at breakfast and at dinner; the web card read 3 October 2026 prints every item at $25.00, confirm on the live card. Breakfast: Eggs Any Style with Toast and Bacon; Popcorn Shrimp with Brabant Potatoes; Vanilla French Toast with Fresh Berries and Whipped Cream; Grilled Cheese Sandwich with Brabant Potatoes, each with a kid's drink, sliced fresh fruit first and a scoop of vanilla ice cream after. High chairs are available. The dress code states no exemption for children: say the house asks for dressy casual and leave enforcement to the host. A fall change was expected and no search shows one, so say 'our current list', never 'our summer list', and confirm the list you are handed on shift.
